Residuals show the model captures the temporal dynamics of y1 and y3 well (lag-1 correlation ≈ 0.984) but carries a systematic bias of ≈ ±0.031; y2 is a near-zero intermediate with negligible absolute error. No numerical failures or gradient-check errors are recorded, but gradient correctness has not been explicitly verified.

Pay particular attention to k2, which sits at 86.7 % of its log-range (5.84e9 out of 5e10); consider whether the upper bound is physically justified or whether the true optimum lies at a different k2/k3 ratio.
recommendations.reason: The single negative Hessian mode (SLOPPINESS) indicates the current point is not a local minimum. k2 at range_fraction 0.867 (PARAMETERS) is near the upper bound, which can create a flat or curved valley that a 5-iteration Adam run cannot traverse. limitations: Gradient checks have not been run in this snapshot; the negative Hessian mode could be a genuine saddle or a numerical artefact, and the evidence cannot distinguish between the two without a probe.

The y2 channel has an extremely small signal (RMSE ≈ 2.3e-05, time correlation 0.449), so it provides very little information for parameter identification; the fit quality for y2 is dominated by the near-zero baseline rather than by the model dynamics.

The systematic bias in y1 and y3 (≈ ±0.031) could arise from initial-condition mismatch, input-timing offset, or a structural model limitation (e.g., missing reaction pathway); the residual statistics alone cannot determine which cause is responsible.

With only 17 data points per channel and a single experiment, identifiability of the three rate constants (k1, k2, k3) is not established; the negative Hessian mode is consistent with a flat or weakly constrained direction in parameter space.
No noise level or measurement uncertainty is specified in the snapshot, so the RMSE values cannot be interpreted as statistically significant or insignificant deviations from the data.
